title: "Library release automation"
subtitle: "ValidMind release notes guides"

Automated `validmind-library` semver release notes (`vX.Y.Z`).

## When are library release drafts automatically generated?

| Scenario | Trigger | `validmind-library` `RELEASE_AUTOMATION` repo variable | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A (tag push)** | When `validmind/validmind-library` receives a new stable semver tag | `vars.RELEASE_AUTOMATION == 'true'` | A [notifier on `validmind-library`](https://github.com/validmind/validmind-library/blob/main/.github/workflows/notify-library-release-notes.yaml){target="_blank"} dispatches `library-release-notes` to the `release-notes` repo |
| **B (`workflow_dispatch`)** — Fallback | A human manually runs `library_release_notes.yml` with a tag | Ungated | Example: `gh workflow run library_release_notes.yml --repo validmind/release-notes -f tag=v2.13.5` |

- Library release automation is triggered by stable `vX.Y.Z` tags only (min. `v2.13.2+` floor); prerelease suffixes (`-rc`, `-alpha`, `-beta`) are rejected by discovery and the library notifier.
- **Patch** vs **feature** follows the new tag relative to the previous stable tag: a patch-only bump (e.g. `v2.13.4` → `v2.13.5`) → patch; a major or minor bump (e.g. `v2.13.5` → `v2.14.0`) → feature. The first in-scope tag is feature when the patch is `.0` and patch otherwise.
- Discovery *skips* a library release when `releases/validmind-library/v{version}/release-notes.qmd` is already on `validmind/release-notes` `main`, or when an open automation PR (release-notes draft and/or documentation preview) is already in flight for that version.
- Re-dispatching the *same* stable tag (for example, running the workflow again) while a draft PR on `automated/library-v{version}` is still open—and the file is not yet on `main` — sets `refresh_in_place` and regenerates on that branch instead of skipping or opening a new PR.

### How are library patch and feature releases different?

| Aspect | Patch release | Feature release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Examples | `v2.13.4` → `v2.13.5` | `v2.13.5` → `v2.14.0` |
| Discover `release_type_hint` | `patch` — semver patch bump vs previous tag, or first in-scope tag with non-zero patch | `feature` — major/minor bump, or first in-scope tag with `.0` patch |
| Zendesk cross-check | Runs automatically | Runs automatically |
| Curated highlights | No generated `*-highlights*` files | Author runs the [Library highlights](highlights.qmd) process after the automated drafts are generated |
| Untagged highlight candidates | Listed in the PR body for human review (advisory only) | Same — candidates do not change the semver `release_type_hint` |


## What happens when library drafts are automatically generated?

### 1. Discovery

- `discover_undocumented_library_releases.py` builds `targets[]`; `generate_library_batch.py` runs the full workflow once per target (each library release tag identified in the delta).
- Per-target `start_tag` and `gap_start_tag` are the previous stable library tag. Fetch, generate, and Zendesk cross-check all use this incremental window — each target documents only PRs since the previous release. Refer to the **Zendesk cross-check review** guide.
- **Stale `discovery.json`:** targets created before the dedupe fix may have a wide `start_tag` without `gap_start_tag`. Batch warns and uses `gap_start_tag` when present; re-dispatch open `automated/*` branches with fresh discover output after merging dedupe fixes — do not reuse pre-fix `discovery.json`.
- Discovery scope is filtered by the library automation floor (`v2.13.2+`). [`LIBRARY_RELEASE_DELTA`](/samples/content-engineering/validmind/release-notes/access-requirements.qmd#repository-variables) is required in `.env` (mirror GitHub) but is discovery-only; it does not widen fetch or generate windows for library targets.

### 2. Automation branch checked out, release notes drafted, and pushed

Before generating, `generate_library_batch.py` runs `_ensure_branch` (`ensure_batch_branch` in `batch_git.py`) so the working tree is on `automated/library-v{version}` (creating or checking out from base when needed). The draft lands on that automation branch — not on `main`.

a. `generate_library_batch.py` runs `generate_library_release_notes.py` with default **`--edit`** (initial LLM cleanup) on partials and library shell. Patch and feature releases both run the Zendesk cross-check in this step before `--edit`.

b. **Written on `release-notes` branch (`automated/library-v{version}`)** — `releases/validmind-library/v{version}/release-notes.qmd` plus `_pr-{n}.qmd` and `pr-{n}.qmd` for all in-scope PRs. *No* curated `*-highlights*` files automatically generated in the initial draft — human authors run the [Library highlights](highlights.qmd) process.

c. **Committed and pushed** to `validmind/release-notes` on `automated/library-v{version}`. No branch is created in `validmind/documentation` at this step.

### 3. Shortcut Story created or reused

Batch automation resolves a Shortcut Story using one of three paths:

| Path | When | How the story is resolved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **create** | First run for a version (no automation branch yet, or new branch from base) | Title search (`Edit v{version} release notes`) → reuse existing story if found, otherwise POST a new chore story |
| **refresh** | Discover sets `refresh_in_place: true` (same tag re-dispatch, `release-notes.qmd` not on `main`, open release-notes PR on `automated/library-v{version}`) | Parse the Shortcut blockquote from the open release-notes PR body (no new POST) |
| **orphan** | Remote automation branch exists but there is no open PR (partial/failed prior run) | Same as **create** — title search then POST or reuse; batch then opens the release-notes PR |

`release-notes` and `documentation` PRs link to the Shortcut Story via the Story blockquote in the PR template. On **refresh**, if the blockquote is missing or malformed, batch falls back to the **create** path (title search) instead of failing.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Shortcut story fields

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Story type | `chore` |
| Title | `Edit v{version} release notes` |
| State | In progress |
| Epic | Automated Release Notes |
| Group | Docs |
| Estimate | 1 |
| Iteration | Current iteration when started |
| Technical Area | Product Documentation |

:::

### 4. Release-notes PR opened

Draft PR on `validmind/release-notes` from `automated/library-v{version}`. Follows the template: `library_pr_body.md`.

On **refresh** (`refresh_in_place`), an open PR already exists — batch updates the branch in place and reuses the existing PR (no new `gh pr create`). On **orphan** resume, batch opens the release-notes PR after Shortcut story resolution.

### 5. Documentation preview deployed

The **Documentation preview** check on the release-notes PR dispatches the reusable preview workflow on `validmind/documentation`. It renders the exact release-notes PR commit and deploys it to `pr_previews/release-notes/pr-{pr_number}`. Every new commit redeploys the same preview URL; no documentation branch or PR is created.

### 6. Slack notification sent

- Posts success or failure to `#release-notes`. Follows templates: `library-success.md`, `library-failure.md`.
- Slack messages use **mrkdwn** (not GitHub Markdown): line 1 is fully bold (`*…*`), links use `<url|label>`, to-do items use `•` bullets, and failure error text is shown in a monospace code block so subprocess output cannot break link formatting.
- `generate_library_batch.py` calls `render_slack_batch_notify.py` per target on success or failure when run locally. In GitHub Actions, batch scripts skip in-process Slack; workflow steps post from `batch_results.json` (`--batch-successes` on success/partial, `--batch-failures` / `--batch-crashed` on failure). Handled per-target failures do not trigger duplicate Slack messages.
- When initial draft `--edit` fails partially, the Slack message includes an edit-skipped line.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}

| **Failure (discovery)** | `#release-notes` | `discover` step fails in `library_release_notes.yml` | *⚠️ Library release notes automation FAILED — v2.13.5*<br>Error (step: `discover`):<br>```<br>Discovery failed<br>```<br>Branches: _none created_ (failed at step: `discover`)<br>Artifacts:<br>• Shortcut story: not created<br>• Release-notes PR: not created<br>• Documentation PR: not created |
| **Failure (batch crashed)** | `#release-notes` | Batch step fails **before** `batch_results.json` is written (true crash only) | Error (step: `generate`):<br>```<br>Batch crashed before writing batch_results.json<br>```<br>— one failure message per target in discovery.json |

:::

## What does a human have to do after the library release automation runs?

### 1. Zendesk cross-check

Library releases run an initial Zendesk cross-check automatically in during initial draft generation — `generate_library_release_notes.py` fetches Shortcut `zendesk_pr_mapping` and GitHub tag-delta, evaluates PR merge windows against library tag timestamps, and injects qualifying customer-linked fixes into the draft before default `--edit` polishes prose.

- Cross-check gaps flagged by automation under **What needs special review?** on the `release-notes` automation PR; gap count also appears in the `#release-notes` Slack success message (`Cross-check gaps: N`).
- Confirm every qualifying fix is in `releases/validmind-library/v{version}/release-notes.qmd` with Zendesk ticket HTML comments; resolve each gap row; spot-check 1–2 tickets in Zendesk for wording and library scope.

### 2. Library feature highlights (feature releases only)

- Run highlight curation on the automation PR branch after initial draft: `curate_library_highlights.py` → `report_library_orphan_prs.py` → `curate_library_highlights.py --materialize`. The initial automated draft does not include `*-highlights*` files.

::: {.callout}
Full guide: [Library highlights](highlights.qmd)

:::

### 3. Human editing & review

- Proofread customer-facing wording in all files that will be visible — refer to the **Editing generated release notes** guide.
- Confirm that `releases/validmind-library-releases.qmd` has been updated with the right `subtitle: "Latest: `v{version}`"` and `date` with your release tag

### 4. Merge release notes

After the **Documentation preview** check passes, merge `release-notes` > `main`. There is no paired documentation PR to clean up or merge. The merge automatically rebuilds the documentation staging site from the updated release-notes source.

### 5. Publish documentation site

After **Publish release notes to documentation staging** passes, push `documentation` to production: `staging` > `prod`.

## Do library drafts automatically get regenerated?

| Scenario | What happens | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Stable refresh** | Re-dispatch with the same tag while an open automation PR exists (and `release-notes.qmd` is not on `main`) sets `refresh_in_place` on the discover target; batch regenerates automation-owned paths and preserves human edits automatically. Feature releases also protect materialized highlight files (`preserve_materialized=not is_patch`). | Same library tag; workflow re-dispatched — not a new tag. |
| **New tag** | A new semver tag opens a new automation PR. | |

::: {.callout}

Discovery auto-detects an open PR and a file not yet on `main` when the same tag is re-dispatched and sets `refresh_in_place: true`: 

- If `releases/validmind-library/v{version}/release-notes.qmd` is not on `main` yet and an automation PR is already open on `automated/library-v{version}`, normal discovery treats that version as *in-flight* and skips it — correct for net-new work, wrong when you want to update the existing draft.
- Generation checks out the existing `automated/library-v{version}` branch, re-fetches Shortcut/Zendesk/GitHub data, regenerates `release-notes.qmd`, commits, and pushes — updating the open PR, not opening a new one. It reuses the existing Shortcut story and PR bodies, and sets up the human-edit protection baseline. Feature releases also protect materialized highlight paths (`preserve_materialized=not is_patch`).

:::
